messages.subject: pcountOpen simulations - dynamics questions
parts:
Hi unmarked folks,

I have some questions about some PcountOpen simulations I’ve been fiddling with. I’m using examples from https://github.com/rbchan/unmarked/blob/master/inst/unitTests/sim.pcountOpen.r#L742

I want to examine the effect of sample size (# of sites) and number of repeat visits on the ‘power’ of a dataset to detect a (3.4% annual) decline in a hypothetical bird population that is fairly rare across the landscape.

Should I be using “dynamics=trend” (Sim11 in link) in PcountOpen for this scenario or are other dynamics possible? For example, why not use “dynamics=constant” and set gamma to zero? How is this different? It says in the Unmarked manual that the “trend” model is an exponential growth model. Perhaps I should be using the Ricker or Gompertz dynamics?

Thanks

Myles Falconer

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] pcountOpen simulations - dynamics questions
parts:
Hi Myles,

The easiest thing to do would be to use dynamics="trend", but really you should think hard about what model best describes the population you are studying and go with that. By the way, the documentation should say "geometric growth", not "exponential growth". I'll make a note to fix that.

Richard
